coverage: All eleven scenes: both pairs of twins, family and city participants, minor tradespeople and named allusions; contextual names and the abbess identity gate.

entities.name: Antipholus of Syracuse
entities.body: Egeon’s son, the visiting twin searching for his mother and brother.

entities.name: Antipholus of Ephesus
entities.body: The twin established in Ephesus, married to Adriana.

entities.name: Dromio of Syracuse
entities.body: The servant travelling with Antipholus of Syracuse; he too has a twin brother.

entities.name: Dromio of Ephesus
entities.body: The servant of Antipholus of Ephesus and twin brother of the other Dromio.

entities.name: Egeon
entities.body: The merchant from Syracuse and father of the Antipholus twins.

entities.name: Adriana
entities.body: Antipholus of Ephesus’s wife and Luciana’s sister.

entities.name: Luciana
entities.body: Adriana’s unmarried sister.

entities.name: Solinus
entities.body: The Duke of Ephesus.

entities.name: Egeon’s wife
entities.body: The mother of Egeon’s twin sons, separated from him in the shipwreck.

snapshots.name: Emilia
snapshots.body: Egeon’s wife and the twins’ mother, now identified as the abbess.

entities.name: The abbess
entities.body: The woman who heads the religious house in Ephesus.

snapshots.name: Emilia, the abbess
snapshots.body: The abbess of Ephesus, Egeon’s wife and the twins’ mother.

entities.name: Angelo
entities.body: The goldsmith making a chain for Antipholus of Ephesus.

entities.name: Balthasar
entities.body: The merchant accompanying Antipholus of Ephesus to dinner.

entities.name: The first merchant
entities.body: The merchant who knows Antipholus of Syracuse and warns him about the city’s laws.

entities.name: The second merchant
entities.body: The merchant to whom Angelo owes money.

entities.name: The courtesan
entities.body: The courtesan at the Porpentine, an acquaintance of Antipholus of Ephesus.

entities.name: Luce
entities.body: A maid in Adriana’s household who speaks from inside the house.

entities.name: Nell
entities.body: The kitchen maid promised to Dromio of Ephesus, also jokingly called Dowsabel.

entities.name: Doctor Pinch
entities.body: The schoolmaster called in as an exorcist.

entities.name: Egeon’s jailer
entities.body: The jailer charged with holding Egeon.

entities.name: The arresting officer
entities.body: The officer enforcing the debt claims involving Angelo and Antipholus of Ephesus.

entities.name: Adriana’s messenger
entities.body: A servant from Adriana’s household who brings her news.

entities.name: The headsman
entities.body: The executioner attending Egeon.

entities.name: The duke’s officers and attendants
entities.body: The officials and attendants accompanying the Duke of Ephesus.

entities.name: Pinch’s assistants
entities.body: The helpers brought in to restrain the men Pinch is treating.

entities.name: Duke Menaphon
entities.body: Solinus’s uncle, the warrior who brought Antipholus of Ephesus to the city.

entities.name: The Duke of Syracuse
entities.body: The ruler whose treatment of Ephesian merchants Solinus describes.

entities.name: Egeon’s factor
entities.body: Egeon’s commercial agent at Epidamnum.

entities.name: The Dromios’ mother
entities.body: The poor woman who gave birth to the twin servants at the same inn as Egeon’s sons.

entities.name: The saddler
entities.body: The tradesman paid for Adriana’s riding equipment.

entities.name: The Centaur’s innkeeper
entities.body: The host at the inn where Antipholus of Syracuse is staying.

entities.name: The tailor
entities.body: The tradesman who takes Antipholus of Syracuse’s measurements.

entities.name: The rope-maker
entities.body: The tradesman from whom Dromio of Ephesus buys a rope.

entities.name: Maud
entities.body: One of the women Dromio of Ephesus calls for at his master’s door.

entities.name: Bridget
entities.body: One of the women Dromio of Ephesus calls for at his master’s door.

entities.name: Marian
entities.body: One of the women Dromio of Ephesus calls for at his master’s door.

entities.name: Cicely
entities.body: One of the women Dromio of Ephesus calls for at his master’s door.

entities.name: Gillian
entities.body: One of the women Dromio of Ephesus calls for at his master’s door.

entities.name: Ginn
entities.body: One of the women Dromio of Ephesus calls for at his master’s door.

entities.name: The ship’s sailors
entities.body: The crew in Egeon’s account of the family’s voyage.

entities.name: The Corinthian fishermen
entities.body: The fishermen involved in the separation of Egeon’s family.

entities.name: The men of Epidamnum
entities.body: The men whom the abbess recalls from the shipwreck.

entities.name: Egeon’s rescuers
entities.body: The crew of the ship that takes Egeon and the children with him aboard.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The deity invoked in the play’s prayers and exclamations.

entities.name: The gods
entities.body: The divine powers invoked by Egeon.

entities.name: Fortune
entities.body: Chance imagined as a power dividing Egeon’s family.

entities.name: Father Time
entities.body: Time personified in the servants’ jokes.

entities.name: Noah
entities.body: The biblical figure associated with the great flood.

entities.name: Adam
entities.body: The first man in Genesis, invoked in Dromio’s joke about the officer’s leather clothes.

entities.name: The Prodigal Son
entities.body: The returning son welcomed with a feast in Jesus’ parable.

entities.name: Satan
entities.body: The devil invoked in the characters’ accusations of demonic activity.

entities.name: Circe
entities.body: The sorceress of Greek myth whose cup transforms men into animals.
